subject: Proportional charge breakdown for seat top-up
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: treasury@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Charge for recent seat top-up — need proportional breakdown

Hi Marcus,

We just provisioned an extra 12 seats against our Dedicated pool on Oct 2nd as part of a short-term ramp. Procurement wants a clear breakdown of the charge they saw on the portal (a one-off line for "capacity adjustment") and whether the VAT you charged is applied to the full monthly price or only the prorated portion.

Can you send:
- A line-item schedule showing how the one-off amount was calculated (per-seat price, days charged)
- VAT % applied and whether Acme should expect a separate VAT invoice
- A corrected PDF invoice we can route to treasury if needed

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
olivia.barnes@acme-corp.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 15:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Charge for recent seat top-up — need proportional breakdown

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the specific asks. Quick answers up front and a PDF + calc attached: please see attached "proration_calculation_acme_10-2026.xlsx" and the adjusted invoice.

Summary: 
- The portal creates a one-off charge that equals: (seat_unit_price) x (number_of_new_seats) x (remaining_days_in_billing_cycle / days_in_billing_cycle). For Acme that produced $2,640.00 on Oct 2.
- VAT (20%) was applied to the prorated amount only — not to a full-month price. We apply tax based on the invoiced taxable amount for the service period billed.
- Attached is an updated invoice (redwood_adjusted_invoice_20261018.pdf) that calls out the prorated line and VAT.

Notes / subtleties:
- If you prefer the charge to be reflected as a credit + monthly invoice instead of a one-off, we can reissue. That changes the payment capture timing but not the total charge so long as seats remain the same for the rest of the cycle.
- For future mid-cycle decreases we also allow negative prorations/credits; let us know if you'd like a standing rule on how those are handled.

Action items:
- Olivia: confirm if treasury needs the invoice to reference PO# 4631 (I can add it).
- Monica: can you confirm VAT registration details for Acme in our system before we finalize the PDF?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Charge for recent seat top-up — need proportional breakdown

Adding a short finance note so there's no ambiguity on VAT treatment.

- We tax based on the billed period and the tax profile assigned to the customer record. For Acme (UK entity, VAT reg), we applied 20% VAT to the prorated service amount as Marcus outlined.
- If Acme is buying through a non-UK legal entity or has reverse-charge documentation, we can mark the invoice accordingly and remove the VAT charge. Please send the VAT registration certificate (or VAT number + country) to finance@redwood.com if you need reverse-charge.

I'll also attach a summary table to the invoice that shows: base prorated charge, VAT amount, total due. Marcus, please route final invoice to Olivia and copy treasury.

Laura Bennett
Head of Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

We also need the invoice to include: PO# 4631, billing address (EU entity), and the VAT number: GB999888777. If you can reissue with invoice_date = 2026-10-05 and attach a PDF that references PO# 4631, we will process payment within standard terms.

Thanks,
Acme Treasury (accounts.payable@acme-corp.com)
